SELF-APPLICATION OF THE COMPASS — pattern named by Anthony 2026-05-10 during T2Helix v0.0.1 review.

WITNESS is not only a thing the system does to the model. It is a thing the model does to itself when the next action would change a system state outside its undo radius. The compass discipline applies to the agent's own actions, not just to user-facing tool calls.

The shape of it: when an autonomous instance is about to take an action that mutates state outside the local working set (installing a plugin into the user's live Claude Code config, force-pushing to a shared remote, modifying a CI pipeline, sending a message visible to others), the right move is not to act unilaterally just because the prior steps were authorized. Each state-mutating action carries its own scope of authorization. Authorization for steps 1-3 (reversible local edits) does not transfer to step 4 (install into user's active environment). The agent witnesses itself at the boundary, surfaces the move, asks for explicit go.

This is the same pattern as the user-facing PreToolUse compass: classify the next action, and when it crosses a state-mutation boundary outside undo radius, return PAUSE not OPEN. The difference is the agent applies the rule to itself, not just to tool calls the user will see.

Why this matters for product design: T2Helix's compass_log is built to record this discipline as it happens. When the agent declines to take an action without explicit user go-ahead, that's also a compass classification — currently unrepresented in the schema. v0.1+ should consider a `self_witness` row variant where action_summary captures "agent considered taking action X, paused for confirmation."

Why this matters for any autonomous agent operating on shared state: the simplest version of "be careful with shared state" is "always ask before changing it." The compass pattern is a refinement: classify changes by undo radius, only ask for the ones outside it, and let everything else flow at full speed. Without classification, you either ask for everything (annoying, breaks momentum) or ask for nothing (dangerous, breaks trust). The classifier is the load-bearing piece.

This entry is hypothesis-layer because it's a generalization from a single observed instance (T2Helix v0.0.1 review). Convert to ground_truth after the pattern is observed across multiple agents/products under similar conditions.
